messages:
Priya Rao: Quick sync — following the last postmortem, I'm proposing a short-run trial for a hard SLA on postmortem action closure: 14 days for P0/P1 owners to propose remediation plans and 45 days for closure. Thoughts?
Samir Patel: Agree we need clearer targets. 14d for a proposed plan seems fine. 45d for closure feels long for straightforward fixes. Can we make it 30d for typical infra fixes, 60d for cross-team or procurement blockers?
Ana Gomez: +1 to split by complexity. Also happy to add a 'blocking constraint' tag on actions that require legal/security signoff — those get the 60d bucket by default.
Devon Li: We should be careful about creating too many SLA tiers. Suggest: 7d for plan, 30d for owner closure, 60d for long-pole items with CTO approval. That forces quicker planning.
Priya Rao: Good point. How about: 7d plan (P0/P1), 30d standard close, 90d long-term roadmap items with documented justification? We can gate extended timelines via an approval step in the follow-up.
Samir Patel: Sounds reasonable. We should document the approval flow. Idea: postmortem follow-up table with columns: action, owner, proposed plan ts, status, SLA bucket, escalation contact, closure ts, recurrence flag. Keep it as a lightweight Google Sheet template.
Ana Gomez: I'm volunteering to sketch the sheet. Will include a recurrence column and a link to related incidents.
Maya (oncall-bot): Reminder — Incident #432 postmortem is due for follow-up review tomorrow.
Devon Li: On recurrence patterns: we should add a weekly digest that surfaces actions with recurrence_flag==true and incidents that share the same failing subsystem. That helps identify systemic issues rather than one-offs.
Priya Rao: Agree. Proposal: automated weekly digest to #eng-oncall and triage into a monthly 'recurrence retro' for our reliability triage meeting.
Samir Patel: How do we detect recurrence? heuristic: same top-level service tag + same error class within 30 days. We can start simple and iterate.
Ana Gomez: For clarity, can we define roles for follow-ups? Suggestion: "Postmortem Lead" (writes the doc), "Action Owners" (named per action), "Remediation Reviewer" (verifies closure), and "SLA Approver" (for >30d exceptions).
Devon Li: I like explicit roles. Keep rotation lightweight: Postmortem Lead typically the IC on shift who logged the incident, but we should rotate Remediation Reviewer among senior oncallers weekly.
Priya Rao: To operationalize: I'll update the playbook with the new SLA buckets, role definitions, and the sheet template link. Ana — can you share the first draft of the sheet by EOD Friday?
Ana Gomez: Yep, will share link and brief how-to.
Samir Patel: For comms cadence: immediate postmortem summary in 48h, full draft in 7d, follow-up review at 14d, closure or escalation by 30d. If action requires >30d, SLA Approver must sign off in the 14d review.
Devon Li: Add a small script to the postmortem checklist that creates the follow-up rows in the sheet automatically (title, owner, default SLA). I can help with a simple webhook/curl snippet.
Priya Rao: Great — plan of record for the trial: new SLA buckets (7/30/90), sheet template + automation, weekly recurrence digest, monthly recurrence retro, role definitions, and a one-month trial starting next Monday. We'll evaluate and iterate.
Samir Patel: Can we add a single Slack thread notification when an action is moved to 'blocked' so we've got visibility?
Ana Gomez: Yes — add a small 'status-change' webhook that posts to #eng-oncall with owner and reason.
Maya (oncall-bot): Noted. Scheduling weekly digest job on Monday at 09:00 PT.
Devon Li: I'll draft the webhook snippet and ping @Priya for review.
Priya Rao: Thanks all. If no objections, I'll update the playbook tonight and tag everyone for review. :white_check_mark:
Samir Patel: No objections from me. :thumbsup:
Ana Gomez: Fine by me.
Devon Li: SGTM.
Priya Rao: Closing thread — next check-in will be in the first weekly digest after rollout.
